home.title:
Making community plugins
look like one product.
home.lede: By the fifth plugin, the interface stops looking like one product: buttons at different heights, every corner radius its own, a dialog that animates here and not there; and when two plugins both want the bottom of the sidebar, whichever loaded first sits on top. The product gives plugins somewhere to run, but no shared answer to how big a control is, how much space goes between two of them, how long a transition runs, or how to draw an icon. This resource supplies it: every number carries its source, and every component is ready to use.

why.title: Why
why.body: Plugins install fine; they just do not add up to one product — that is why this repository exists.

why.title: Why plugins do not look like one product
why.lede: Each plugin is fine on its own; together they stop looking like one product. The reason is plain: there is an interface to install into, but no shared answer for what a plugin should look like once it is in. The three sections below cover what the product already gives you, what you will run into, and where these numbers come from.
why.officialTitle: What the product already gives you
why.scopeTitle: What this repository will not do

items.tokens: A ready-made set of values for colour, type, radius, spacing and elevation, in light and dark.
items.primitives: Buttons, switches, inputs, menus and notices already ship with the product, along with one explicit instruction: do not copy a control that already exists.
items.seats: A list of everywhere UI can go: what each spot is for, how many plugins fit, and whether it covers official UI.
items.icons: An icon set with a consistent naming scheme and size families, so a redrawn glyph does not drift.
items.aesthetics: It does not judge how things look. It keeps things consistent and usable; it does not claim one style is better.
items.force: It does not force anyone to change their code. It is a shared reference for people who opt in.
items.invent: It does not invent numbers. Every size, gap and duration can name its source, and where no authority exists it says so.

gaps.layoutClaim: Two plugins both want their button at the bottom of the sidebar; whichever loaded first sits on top.
gaps.layoutBody: How much room a plugin may take, and how it shares space with the conversation, has no shared answer. Each plugin follows its own reading, and together they crowd: one covers the conversation, another leaves a gap nobody uses.
gaps.orderClaim: The order of plugins in one spot can change when you reload.
gaps.orderBody: Spots that take several plugins sort them by order, but nothing says what to put there. The default is 0, so whichever loads first goes first — the user sees an arbitrary stack, not the important one on top.
gaps.motionClaim: One plugin closes a panel in 100 milliseconds; the next takes 350.
gaps.motionBody: How long an expand, a collapse or a popover should take has no shared scale. Both numbers are defensible on their own; side by side they look like two different products.
gaps.iconGeometryClaim: A hand-drawn icon gives itself away next to an official one.
gaps.iconGeometryBody: How thick the stroke should be, how it lines up with its neighbours, how much air it needs — there is no reference to check against. Fine alone, rough in a row.
gaps.conflictClaim: When two plugins want the same spot, nothing tells you.
gaps.conflictBody: The later one simply covers the earlier one. Nothing is missing from the interface and nothing logs an error — you find out from user reports.

proof.overlay: 14 plugins occupy shell.overlay in the official UI, and 11 of them never say where they belong in the order. They all fall to the default 0, so the stacking follows load order — reload the same machine and the order can change.
proof.settings: 11 plugins occupy settings.section, and 3 of them all declare order 40. Which of those three comes first is equally unexplained.

why.asideNote: Both figures were counted on this machine on 2026-10-01; the raw snapshot is in data/raw/occupancy-2026-10-01.json. A different machine, or a different set of enabled plugins, gives different numbers.
why.closing: This is not one plugin's fault. With no shared answers, everyone makes a reasonable choice and the sum still looks like this. The repository does two things: it fills in the numbers and the practice that were missing, and it makes the collisions visible.

components.title: Reusable source
components.lede: Each component is a standalone React implementation built on official tokens, with where its numbers came from and when to use it. Take it and go.
components.docSpecNote: This one is for engineers and agents: where the numbers came from, the API, the tokens, and the constraints a machine can check.
components.chineseOnly: This component's documentation is currently Chinese-only.
components.usage: The component directory is itself an npm package you can install, or you can copy just the folder you need into your plugin.

seats.title: Seat directory
seats.lede: The product has {n} places a plugin can put UI. Your interface lives in exactly one of them — choosing the wrong one costs more than writing the wrong style.
seats.riskyNote: {n} of them cover official UI once you occupy them. Use those only when you really mean to replace that part of the interface.

kinds.single: single — one occupant only; a later registration covers an earlier one
kinds.list: list — as many as you like, sorted by order from low to high
kinds.keyed: keyed — handed out by key, one slot each
kinds.chain: chain — a selector decides; the whole chain can be replaced

scopes.root: root — global, present even with no session
scopes.maybe: session-maybe — tied to a session, but can be empty
scopes.session: session — appears once a session is selected

seats.orderNote: Start with the list spot whose meaning fits best; if none does, fall back to a single spot; leave the ones that cover official UI for last.

icons.title: Official icon set
icons.lede: {n} icons, lifted from the product exactly as they are, shapes untouched. Naming: ic_ds_<name>_<style>_<size>. Click one to copy its SVG.
icons.familyTail: If you draw your own, match the stroke weight and the breathing room of the icons beside it.
icons.why: Mismatched icons are where a plugin interface gives itself away. This set already has its weight and padding worked out; reusing it is less work than drawing something close enough, and it stays even.

tokens.title: Design tokens
tokens.lede: {palette} colour values back {aliases} named colours. Use the names, not the values — light and dark are already worked out.
tokens.usageNote: Reach for a token name, never a hard-coded value. The first thing to give way in dark mode is a colour written into the stylesheet.
tokens.depth: Express depth with background layers (bg-base → bg-layer-1 → bg-layer-2 → bg-overlay), not with shadows. A shadow is the exception, not the default.
tokens.source: Values come straight from the theme definition inside the product's client bundle, one set per theme, unmodified.
